newsitem.title: UK: VLCCs stay firm, other tankers languish.
newsitem.headline: VLCCs stay firm, other tankers languish.

text.p: Very large crude carriers (VLCCs) stayed firm on Tuesday while rates for smaller tankers remained in the doldrums, brokers said.
VLCCs from the Middle East to Singapore fetched a firm W70, with some brokers predicting they could rise to W75 by the end of the week, while to Japan they continued to be fixed at W75/77.5.
"VLCCs to Singapore have got to start moving up. They should get W75 by the end of the week, hopefully," one broker said, pointing to tight tonnage and good demand.
VLCCs to Japan were last done at W77.5, a year high, according to Reuters Tanker Industry Index.
The 260,000 tonne New Vitality was fixed on a Mideast/Japan trip at W74.5 for Tonen, while the 250,000 tonne Asian Progress fetched W75 to South Korea for LG-Caltex.
At least one VLCC was reported fixed from the Mediterranean to the U.K./Cont, the 280,000 tonne Arosa done on a Sidi Kreir/UKC voyage at W69 for BP.
the 260,000 tonne Boree was said done West Africa/U.S. Gulf at W2.5 for three consecutive voyages for Arcadia.
The Suezmax market, meanwhile, languished around year lows at about W85 from West Africa to USAC, compared with a year high of W107.8, Reuters figures show.
Cross-Med Suezmaxes were also in the doldrums at W80/85.
The Aframax (80,000 tonne) market fared no better, with cross-Med voyages continuing to fetch W120 and inter-UKC W100.
In the Caribs/upcoast markets, 70,000 tonne crude cargoes slipped about five points to W125 while 50,000 fuel oil parcels also edged down to W170 on low volume, brokers said.
European fuel oil was little changed, with 25,000 tonnes cross-Med at W180 and inter-UKC up slightly at W210.
